_readme: EVERY WORD THE WATCH PRINTS, AND WHERE IT PRINTS IT.
The watch was the last surface outside the copy contract. Its words were typed in two
places nobody else reads — `garmin/resources/strings/strings.xml` for the settings and
the FIT field names, and `"…"` literals inside the Monkey C that draws the pages — so a
wording decided on the phone reached the wrist only when somebody remembered. This file
is the meeting place, and `garmin/tools/make_strings.py` is the generator:
python3 garmin/tools/make_strings.py            # write the strings.xml files
python3 garmin/tools/make_strings.py --check     # exit 1 while one is stale
It writes `garmin/resources/strings/strings.xml`, `garmin/resources-dev/base/strings/
strings.xml` and `garmin/source/ui/Words.mc`, which is how a page reaches a word: one
`WatchUi.loadResource` per string at page construction, never per draw.
AN ENTRY IS:
id      the Rez string id. Unique across both streams.
text    the word itself, hand-authored HERE.
where   where a rider reads it. Required, and the reason the inventory is worth having.
term    THE GLOSSARY ID THIS WORD SPELLS (docs/copy/glossary.json). Its presence is
what hands the string to the glossary lint: `web/tools/verify_glossary.py`
fails unless `text` is one of that term's own spellings — its `term`, its
`short`, or one of its `labels`. A string with no `term` is not a metric
label (a settings row, a page state, a menu), and the lint says so itself:
a word that IS a glossary spelling and names no term fails too.
why     REQUIRED where `term` is set and `text` is not one of that term's spellings.
The watch is held to the contract at its own width, not excused from it, so
every divergence is one line saying what the glass could not take. Every one
is printed on each run of the lint, because an exemption nobody reads becomes
the rule.
var     the Monkey C global the pages draw it through, or a list of them where one
word is drawn in more than one place. Its presence puts the string in the
generated `Words.mc`; a string with no `var` is drawn by Garmin (a settings
row, a FIT field name, the launcher) and no page loads it.
pad     "leading" | "trailing" | "both" — a space the generator adds around the word.
The counts either side of " of " are drawn in a number font and the word at
FONT_XTINY, so the two are not on one baseline run and the gaps have to be
part of the small string. XML is no place to keep a significant space.
note    an XML comment written above the entry, for a fact the next author needs.
stream  "base" (every stream) or "dev" (the dev listing only). Default base.
THE SURFACE IS DERIVED, not declared, so that it cannot disagree with the entry it is
written on: a string with a `var` is a word a PAGE draws; an id beginning `FitUnit` is a
unit; an id beginning `Fit` is a GARMIN CONNECT FIELD name; an id beginning `AppName` is
the launcher; everything else is a Garmin Connect settings row. The glossary lint reads
the first two of those — a page word and a Connect field name are the two places a number
gets a name, and they are the two that collided on 20 September 2026. A settings row is a
question, not a label, and is judged by docs/copy/check_voice.py instead.
THE DIVERGENCES (the `why` lines below) are the round's findings, 22 September
2026. Two were aligned in the same round because they are Garmin Connect rows rather
than pages and no glass had a vote: the session share is `On foil` now, not `Foil %`,
which is the spelling the label table decided on 15 September and every other surface
already printed, and the record field is `Best 2 s`, which is the one spelling of that
window in the product. The other twelve are pages, and a page is 240 px wide.

strings.note: The launcher name, one per stream. docs/channels.md, "Telling the channels apart".
The settings rows, in the order Garmin Connect draws them (resources/settings/settings.xml).

strings.text: Show cell labels. Off: glyph only

Records full wrist motion for pump analysis on the phone. The activity file gets roughly 20x larger, so the transfer to Garmin Connect after saving can take several minutes. Leave off for fast transfers.
A clean jibe gets its own rising three-tick buzz. Clean: you flew through and held your speed. Off: every turn gets the plain outcome buzz.
Every buzz also paints. The glass flashes the verdict for 1.5 s. A line at the top keeps the last one for 20 s.

strings.note: ALIGNED 22 Sep 2026: this row said `Foil %`, which is the spelling the label table retired on 15 September. It is the one place it survived (MetricGlossary.swift says so in its own comment). A Connect row has no chord to fit, so there was nothing to trade.
ALIGNED 22 Sep 2026: `Best 2s speed` said the window twice and spelled it a third way. `Best 2 s` is design/tokens.json's one spelling of that window, and the unit column already says cm/s.

The Garmin Connect row for session field 34. No WATCH page prints this share any more (0.9.19 — the pages print the phone's outcome ladder), but the field is still written and Connect still needs a word for it: `Speed kept` is what that number is. docs/fit-schema.md, the box on field 34.

Fields 35 and 36 folded into the packed `takeoff_pack` (55), so their two labels — FitTakeoffAttempts / FitTakeoffSuccesses — had no FIT contribution left to name and went with them (0.9.19). A packed field carries one label, not three.
0.9.16: the page SET. The only page control a release or beta watch has; the per-page editor's strings moved to resources-dev/base/strings/ with its settings.
